espn-603993.headline: Argentina keep finishing one score short
beats: Argentina's last four Tests: beaten 31–24 by England, 17–10 by South Africa and 27–21 by Australia, then a 28–28 draw with Australia. Their one win this year came against Wales.

They reach Dublin without Santiago Carreras, 70 caps, or prop Thomas Gallo, both injured. Facundo Isa is back after missing international duty in 2024 and 2026, his only Argentina games since then coming in July 2025.

Ireland have not played since July, when New Zealand beat them 40–21. Before that they won four straight, one of them 33–31 in Australia. Lose here and Ireland drop to fourth in the world, below France.
Seven points or fewer has separated Argentina from a result in three of their last four. Ireland would like the gap wider than that.

espn-603994.headline: Australia put 42 on South Africa and 57 on Italy
beats: South Africa's last Test was a 38–42 defeat away to Australia in September, and they scored six tries in it. Italy went to Australia in July, lost 10–57, and have not played since.

South Africa top the Nations Championship on points difference alone, level with New Zealand on 15. Italy are 11th without a point, having conceded 47 and 57 in consecutive weeks. A side chasing margin before a trip to France on 13 November could not draw a kinder profile.

The last meeting, on 15 November 2025, finished Italy 14–32 South Africa in Italy. Win this time and Italy hand New Zealand first place in the world rankings, which would be an awkward thing to explain on the way to Paris.
Italy's last win was 23–18 over England in March. Since then Australia have shown both defences can leak 40. Only one of them is top of the table.

espn-603995.headline: Thirty-three attempts, two draws, no Scotland win
beats: This is the 34th meeting. New Zealand have won 31, and the draws of 1964 and 1983 are as close as Scotland have come. Gregor Townsend has lost all three as coach, all in Edinburgh, by eight, eight and five.

Last November Scotland trailed 17–0, levelled at 17–17, then lost 25–17. Of his playing days Townsend says, "As a player, I don't think we ever felt we could win the game." Of the job now: "I've not felt that as a coach."
New Zealand lost three in a row to South Africa, then put 50 and 43 on Australia in October. Scotland have not played since beating Fiji in July, a tour on which they conceded 42 and 38.
Win and Scotland go above England into fifth in the world. Nobody at Murrayfield will be thinking about the ranking.

sources.title: Townsend never felt he could beat All Blacks as a player, but as a coach...

espn-603996.headline: Wales won by a point last year. The gap is smaller now
beats: Their last meeting, in Cardiff on 15 November 2025, went to Wales 24–23. They return to the same ground 10th and 12th in the world, with almost nothing between their ratings.

Wales last played in July and were beaten 43–0 by South Africa without scoring a try. Japan beat Fiji to win the Pacific Nations Cup in September, then lost 34–28 to them at home on 24 October and dropped three places.

Any Japan win takes them above Wales and Italy and leaves Wales 12th at best. It would also lift Japan over Wales in the Nations Championship, where one point separates them now. Steve Tandy has made a late call-up of Macs Page, whose Scarlets boss Nigel Davies expects a debut soon.
A week later Wales host New Zealand and Japan go to England. Neither is the fixture you would pick for a bounce-back.

espn-603997.headline: South Africa are next. France swear they haven't noticed
beats: Mickael Guillard says France have not discussed South Africa, who come to France the following week. One reason may be across the halfway line: his club team-mate Jiuta Wainiqolo, whom he calls "a phenomenon".

Fiji are bottom of the Nations Championship without a point, having conceded 73 to England in July. They also beat Japan 34–28 in Tokyo on 24 October, and Jake White, the new head coach, took ten of that side straight to camp in Lyon.
France have scored six tries in each of their last two Tests and beat Fiji 34–21 at home on 15 November 2025. A Fiji win would still drop France to fifth in the world, below England.
Lose here, and France will have plenty to discuss before South Africa.

espn-603998.headline: Ten Tests since July meets three days in Bagshot
beats: England's last Test was a 31–24 win in Argentina on 18 July. Their preparation since has been one camp, squeezed between Prem weekends, before the players went back to their clubs.
Australia arrive battle-hardened, which cuts both ways. They beat South Africa 42–38 in September, then conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in a fortnight.

Fin Smith started at 10 in all three of England's July Tests. He damaged a calf playing for Northampton, and Charlie Atkinson has been called up as cover. Lose, and England drop to seventh while Australia go up to fifth.
Borthwick calls his approach "doing more of less". Last November, at home, less was enough: England won 25–7.

espn-603999.headline: Beat South Africa and France hand New Zealand top spot
beats: South Africa have been top of the world rankings since 31 August, but they hold it by one result. A France win in Saint-Denis drops them to second, behind New Zealand, while France climb only to third.

The last time France hosted them, on 8 November 2025, South Africa won 32–17. Their most recent Test was a 42–38 loss to Australia. France have scored 42 in each of their last two, and conceded 50 to Scotland in March. Nobody should expect a low-scoring game.
Rassie Erasmus has built his November squad around pace. Nick Mallett reckons the no-frills bolter Yaqeen Ahmed offers something Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu does not.
In New Zealand, Sir John Kirwan is still working out how to combat South Africa up front. The quickest answer this month may be to let France do it.

espn-604000.headline: Italy haven't won since March. Argentina have Montoya back
beats: Italy's last win was 23–18 over England at home in March. Four defeats have followed, including 57 and 47 conceded to Australia and New Zealand in July. Gonzalo Quesada's own summary of November was "Situazione difficile".

Felipe Contepomi has named his strongest roster of the year, with captain Julián Montoya among more than a dozen returning players. Santiago Carreras and Thomas Gallo are out long term, and Argentina reach Genova via a Test with Ireland in Dublin on 6 November.
Argentina have one win in six this year and drew 28–28 with Australia in September, so the visitors are not without frailties. A home win would lift Italy to ninth in the world, above Fiji and Wales.
Fiji come to Udine a week later, level with Italy on no points. Lose here, and that becomes the match for last place.

espn-604001.headline: Wales scored a record 26 in Cardiff and lost by 26
beats: Last November New Zealand won here 52–26, which Reuters recorded as their 34th consecutive win over Wales. Rogers scored a hat-trick, the first against New Zealand since 2004, and it changed nothing.

Wales have not played since July, when South Africa beat them 43–0 away. New Zealand put 50 and 43 past Australia in October. Their only defeats under Dave Rennie, in charge since March, have come against South Africa.

Rennie has used over 50 players in 2026, and Sir John Kirwan sees November as his final month to experiment before the World Cup. Saula Ma'u, uncapped and around 22st, is in the squad. Win and Wales go above Fiji to ninth, a modest reward for ending a run that long.
New Zealand head to England a week later, level on points with South Africa at the top of the table. They would rather the streak did not end on the way.
